Empirical Research Plan  

================================================================  
1. Identification Strategy  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Primary strategy: Difference-in-difference-in-differences (DDD).  

• Dimension 1 (Time): Pre-program spells (01/1986–12/1987) vs. program-period spells (08/1989–07/1991).  
• Dimension 2 (Space): Residence in one of the 28 REBP districts (“eligible region”) vs. residence in a neighbouring non-eligible district on the other side of the border.  
• Dimension 3 (Age): Unemployed entrants aged ≥ 50 at the start of the spell (“age-eligible”) vs. entrants aged 46–49 (“age-ineligible”).  

The triple difference nets out (i) aggregate macro shocks common to all workers, (ii) border-specific shocks common to both sides of the border, and (iii) age-specific shocks that are common across regions. Remaining differences are attributed to the REBP.  

Why DDD is appropriate  
• The reform created two sharp, binary assignment rules (region and age). Combining them with a pre/post comparison isolates the causal effect under a plausibly satisfied “common trends” assumption.  
• Both assignment variables are observed precisely in the registers.  
• Strong first stage: potential benefit length jumps from 30 → 209 weeks for the treated cells.  
• The large sample size and rich controls allow precision and numerous robustness checks (event-study, spatial or age RDD around the two cut-offs).  

Robustness/secondary strategies  
• Spatial RDD: Compare spells in communities within ±30 minutes of driving time from the border; running variable = signed travel time.  
• Age RDD: Compare entrants within ±18 months of the 50th birthday, in eligible districts only.  
These will serve as validity checks of the main DDD estimates.  

================================================================  
2. Treatment and Control Definitions  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Treatment indicator Tij = EligibleRegioni × (Agei ≥ 50) × Postt  

Control observations are all other combinations of the three binary dimensions. In the baseline DDD regression, the coefficient on Tij identifies the ATE on those who satisfy all three criteria.  

Timing  
• Reform start date: 1 June 1988. To avoid contamination from implementation lags, the program window starts 1 August 1989 and ends 31 July 1991.  
• Spells are assigned to the “post” period if their start date ∈ [1 Aug 1989, 31 Jul 1991].  

RDD variables (for robustness)  
• Spatial running variable: signed travel-time (minutes) from worker’s community centroid to closest point on the eligibility border (negative = ineligible side). Cut-off 0.  
• Age running variable: exact age in days at spell start; cut-off 50 years.  

================================================================  
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
A1. Parallel trends (in the absence of treatment) across the four age-region cells on either side of the reform.  
– Plausibility: The steel-restructuring districts were chosen in 1987, but both sides of the border are subject to the same nationwide labour-market institutions and macro shocks. Using only spells within a narrow border band (±30 min) strengthens credibility.  

A2. No anticipatory behaviour that differs by treatment status.  
– Plausibility: The exact generosity of the REBP and its continuation were not certain ex-ante; moreover, eligibility is locked at unemployment entry, limiting scope for strategic timing of layoffs. We will still test for bunching right after the 50th birthday.  

A3. Stable unit treatment value (no spillovers).  
– Plausibility: Job-search externalities across districts could violate this, but geographic frictions inside Austria (commuting costs, unemployment office jurisdiction) make large cross-border spillovers unlikely. We test for displacement effects in vacancies along the border.  

A4. Treatment assignment is as-good-as-random conditional on fixed effects and controls.  
– Plausibility: Residence was required for min. six months; movers right before unemployment could bias results. We exclude movers in the previous year and control for pre-spell community employment growth.  

================================================================  
4. Main Threats and Mitigation  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Threat 1: Differential pre-trends.  
Mitigation:  
• Plot event-study coefficients for ­10 to ­2 quarters before the reform; test joint significance.  
• Include community×age-group fixed effects and community×year linear trends.  

Threat 2: Selective migration into REBP districts.  
Mitigation:  
• Drop individuals who moved community in the 24 months before spell start.  
• Show balance tests on observables (earnings, tenure) between movers and stayers.  

Threat 3: Other policy changes differentially affecting older workers (e.g. early-retirement rules).  
Mitigation:  
• The early-retirement rules are nationwide and time-invariant during 1986-1995; they are absorbed by age dummies.  
• As an external check, estimate placebo DDD on the 54–58 age group (always ineligible for REBP) to verify zero effects.  

================================================================  
5. R Code Outline  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
```r
# 0. Packages ---------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)   # fast I/O
library(fixest)       # regressions with many FEs
library(rdrobust)     # RDD robustness

# 1. Load data --------------------------------------------------
assd <- fread("assd_unemp_spells.csv")   # spell-level ASSD extract
aur  <- fread("aur_community_data.csv")  # residence & distance

dt <- merge(assd, aur, by = c("spell_id"))

# 2. Sample restrictions ---------------------------------------
dt <- dt[year(start_date) %in% 1986:1991]        # pre & program windows
dt <- dt[age_start >= 46 & age_start <= 53]      # focus age band
dt <- dt[exp_ratio >= 0.7]                       # continuous careers
dt <- dt[steel_sector == 0]                      # exclude steel

# Drop recent movers
dt <- dt[moved_last24m == 0]

# 3. Variable construction -------------------------------------
# Time window dummies
dt[, post := fifelse(start_date >= as.IDate("1989-08-01") &
                     start_date <= as.IDate("1991-07-31"), 1L, 0L)]
# Age & region eligibility
dt[, age50 := as.integer(age_start >= 50)]
dt[, eligible_reg := as.integer(rebp_district == 1)]

# Triple-interaction treatment
dt[, treat := post * age50 * eligible_reg]

# Outcome variables
dt[, unemp_weeks := pmin(duration_weeks, 209L)]
dt[, time_to_job := time_to_next_job_weeks]

# Fixed effects
dt[, cell_fe := interaction(community_id, age50)]

# 4. Main DDD regression ---------------------------------------
est1 <- feols(unemp_weeks ~ treat + 
                post:age50 + post:eligible_reg + age50:eligible_reg +
                post + age50 + eligible_reg |
                cell_fe + quarter_start,
              data = dt, cluster = ~community_id)

summary(est1)

# 5. Event-study specification ---------------------------------
dt[, rel_q := as.integer((yearquarter(start_date) - 
                           yearquarter("1988 Q2")))]
# Drop Q0 & Q+1– allow for phase-in
dt <- dt[rel_q %between% c(-10L, 12L)]

est2 <- feols(unemp_weeks ~ i(rel_q, age50*eligible_reg, ref = -1) |
                cell_fe, 
              data = dt, cluster = ~community_id)

iplot(est2, ci = TRUE, ref.line = 0)

# 6. Spatial RDD robustness (±30-min band) ---------------------
band <- 30   # minutes
rdd <- dt[abs(distance_border) <= band & post == 1 & age50 == 1]

rd_res <- rdrobust(y = rdd$unemp_weeks, x = rdd$distance_border,
                   c = 0, p = 1, cluster = rdd$community_id)
summary(rd_res)
```

================================================================  
6. Expected Results  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Economic theory (search models with liquidity effects) predicts that longer potential benefits reduce job-finding hazards, increasing unemployment duration. Given a seven-fold increase in potential duration, we expect:  

• Men 50–53: +25–35 weeks in registered unemployment (≈ 85–115 % increase).  
• Women 50–53: Possibly larger (+35–45 weeks) because REBP can bridge them directly to early retirement at 54, lowering their job-search incentives.  

We expect stronger responses in the upper tail of the duration distribution (spell P75, P90).  

================================================================  
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DiD / DDD)  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
C1: Pre-treatment parallel trends visually and statistically supported …… 1  
C2: No composition changes (migration, selection)  …………………… 0.5  
C3: No differential anticipation/bunching  …………………………… 0.5  
C4: Stable treatment/control classification across time  ……………… 1  
C5: No spillovers or interference  ………………………………………… 0.5  

Total ≈ 3.5 / 5 – credible but depends on documented pre-trend balance and migration checks.
